chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), narrated:

Regarding a man who emancipated his slave, and the slave had wealth. For whom is the wealth of the slave? He (peace be upon him) said: If he (the master) knew that the slave had wealth, it would follow him (the slave), otherwise it belongs to the emancipator (the master).

key_terms.لِلْمُعْتِقِ: For the emancipator (the master who freed the slave)

ai.seo_question: Who owns the wealth of a slave when he is emancipated by his master?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of prominent jurists like Zurarah and reported from the Imams, clarifies the financial rights of a freed slave (mukatab) within Shia fiqh. It establishes that the master's knowledge of the slave's existing wealth is the decisive factor: if known, the wealth stays with the slave to ensure his financial independence; if unknown, it reverts to the master as compensation for the loss of servitude. This ruling underscores the principle that emancipation should not unjustly enrich the master at the expense of the slave's accumulated assets.
